For an ordered register of $n$ qubits, a **stabilizer subgroup** is an abelian
subgroup $S$ of the Hermitian $n$-qubit Pauli operators such that
$-I\notin S$. The binary label of a phase-aware Pauli $P(k,x,z)$ is
$(x,z)\in\mathbb F_2^{2n}$. Define the **rank** of $S$ by

$$\operatorname{rank}(S):=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{span} \{(x,z):P(k,x,z)\in S\}.$$

The binary label convention and commutation form are supplied by the cited
Pauli items. [[lem-qc-stabilizer-subgroup-label-space-and-order]] proves that
this label span is isotropic, its dimension is independent of any generating
set, and $|S|=2^{\operatorname{rank}(S)}$. Matrix multiplication gives the
phase-aware Pauli group operation by
[[thm-qc-pauli-product-and-adjoint]]. For $n=0$, the Pauli group is the
empty-register convention of [[def-qc-pauli-group-on-zero-qubits]].

Let $S$ be a stabilizer subgroup on $n\ge0$ qubits and let
$\lambda(P(k,x,z))=(x,z)$. Then $\lambda|_S$ is injective, its image $L$ is an
isotropic $\mathbb F_2$-subspace, the rank $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L$ depends only
on $S$ and not on a generating list, and
$|S|=2^{\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L}$.

Let $F$ be a field, let $m,n,p\in\mathbb N$, and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and
$B=(b_{jk})\in M_{n\times p}(F)$. Their **matrix product** is the matrix
$AB\in M_{m\times p}(F)$ whose entries are

$$(AB)_{ik}:=\sum_{j\in n}a_{ij}b_{jk}.$$

The sum is the finite sum in the additive commutative monoid of $F$. If $n=0$,
it is the empty sum, so $AB$ is the zero matrix of shape $m$ by $p$.

The **identity matrix** $I_n\in M_n(F)$ has entry $1$ when $i=j$ and entry $0$
when $i\ne j$. In particular, $I_0$ is the unique empty matrix in $M_0(F)$.

All complex inner products in this track use the root convention: they are
linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second
([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). For vectors $x,y$ in the same
space, define the Dirac pairing by

$$\langle x|y\rangle_D:=\langle y,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}.$$

The ket $|x\rangle$ denotes the vector $x$. The bra $\langle x|$ denotes the
linear functional $z\mapsto\langle z,x\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}$.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H,K$, vectors $y\in H$ and
$x\in K$, define the rank-one linear map

$$|x\rangle\langle y|:H\to K,\qquad z\mapsto\langle z,y\rangle_{H,\mathrm{root}}x.$$

Given ordered orthonormal bases of $H$ and $K$, its coordinate matrix is
$[x][y]^\dagger$, where $[x]$ and $[y]$ are the corresponding coordinate
columns and $M^\dagger:=\overline M^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose.
The coordinate assertion is established in
[[thm-qc-dirac-notation-coordinate-identity]].

derivations.claim: Since every $g$ is Hermitian, $\Pi_S^\dagger=\Pi_S$. In the product $\Pi_S^2=|S|^{-2}\sum_{g,h\in S}gh$, each $k\in S$ occurs exactly $|S|$ times: for each $g$ there is exactly one $h=g^{-1}k\in S$. Therefore $\Pi_S^2=|S|^{-1}\sum_{k\in S}k=\Pi_S$.

For any $s\in S$, left multiplication $g\mapsto sg$ permutes $S$, so $s\Pi_S=\Pi_S$. Hence every vector in $\operatorname{im}\Pi_S$ is fixed by every $s\in S$. Conversely if $s v=v$ for all $s\in S$, then $\Pi_Sv=|S|^{-1}\sum_{s\in S}sv=v$. Thus $\operatorname{im}\Pi_S=\mathcal C(S)$.

If $\mathcal C(S)=\mathbb C\psi$ with $\|\psi\|=1$, then $\Pi_S$ is a self-adjoint idempotent onto that line. Its kernel is orthogonal to its image: for $u=\Pi_S w$ and $\Pi_Sv=0$, $\langle u,v\rangle=\langle w,\Pi_Sv\rangle=0$. Therefore it is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb C\psi$. By [A1] that projection is $|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$.

For a stabilizer subgroup $S$ on $n$ qubits, the finite operator average

$$\Pi_S:=\frac{1}{|S|}\sum_{g\in S}g$$

is self-adjoint and idempotent, and its image is exactly the common $+1$ fixed
space $\mathcal C(S)$. If this image is the span of a unit vector $\psi$, then
$\Pi_S=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ under the root-linear-first Dirac convention.

Let $S$ be a stabilizer subgroup on $n\ge0$ qubits and let
$\lambda(P(k,x,z))=(x,z)$. Then $\lambda|_S$ is injective, its image $L$ is an
isotropic $\mathbb F_2$-subspace, the rank $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L$ depends only
on $S$ and not on a generating list, and
$|S|=2^{\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L}$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

The zero-qubit register is the empty tensor product $H_0=\mathbb C$ with
identity operator $I_{H_0}$. Define

$$P_0(k):=i^kI_{H_0}\quad(k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z),\qquad
\mathcal P_0:=\{P_0(k):k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}.$$

Then $P_0(k)P_0(\ell)=P_0(k+\ell)$ and $P_0(k)^*=P_0(-k)$, so
$\mathcal P_0$ is the cyclic scalar Pauli group of order four. Its Hermitian
elements are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$. The binary-label space
$\mathbb F_2^0\times\mathbb F_2^0$ is the zero space, and the label of each
$P_0(k)$ is its unique element.

This supplies the empty-register case when an item uses Pauli notation whose
general positive-wire convention is stated separately.

For an ordered register of $n$ qubits, a **stabilizer subgroup** is an abelian
subgroup $S$ of the Hermitian $n$-qubit Pauli operators such that
$-I\notin S$. The binary label of a phase-aware Pauli $P(k,x,z)$ is
$(x,z)\in\mathbb F_2^{2n}$. Define the **rank** of $S$ by

$$\operatorname{rank}(S):=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\operatorname{span} \{(x,z):P(k,x,z)\in S\}.$$

The binary label convention and commutation form are supplied by the cited
Pauli items. [[lem-qc-stabilizer-subgroup-label-space-and-order]] proves that
this label span is isotropic, its dimension is independent of any generating
set, and $|S|=2^{\operatorname{rank}(S)}$. Matrix multiplication gives the
phase-aware Pauli group operation by
[[thm-qc-pauli-product-and-adjoint]]. For $n=0$, the Pauli group is the
empty-register convention of [[def-qc-pauli-group-on-zero-qubits]].

For a square matrix $A=(a_{ij})\in M_n(F)$, its **trace** is the sum of its
diagonal entries,

$$\operatorname{tr}(A):=\sum_{i\in n}a_{ii}.$$

For $n=0$, this is the empty sum, so the unique empty matrix has trace $0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

If $P:V\to V$ is an idempotent endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space over a field $k$, then $\operatorname{tr}(P)=(\dim_k\operatorname{im}P)\cdot1_k$. In positive characteristic this equality does not in general determine the integer rank from the trace.

Let $V=\mathbb F_2^{2n}$ have the standard symplectic form
$\omega((x,z),(x',z'))=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'$. If $L\le V$ is isotropic and
$r=\dim L$, then

$$\dim L^\perp=2n-r.$$

Consequently $r\le n$, and if $r=n$ then

$$L^\perp:=\{v\in V:\omega(v,\ell)=0\text{ for every }\ell\in L\}=L.$$

Let $(M,+,0)$ be a commutative monoid and let all index sets below be finite.

1. If $h:T\to S$ is a bijection and $a:S\to M$, then $\sum_{t\in T}a_{h(t)}=\sum_{s\in S}a_s$.
2. If $S$ and $T$ are disjoint and $a:S\cup T\to M$, then $\sum_{u\in S\cup T}a_u=\sum_{s\in S}a_s+\sum_{t\in T}a_t$.
3. If $a:S\times T\to M$, then
   $$\sum_{(s,t)\in S\times T}a_{s,t}=\sum_{s\in S}\left(\sum_{t\in T}a_{s,t}\right)=\sum_{t\in T}\left(\sum_{s\in S}a_{s,t}\right).$$

derivations.claim: By [F1], [F2], and [F10], $0\le r\le n$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_S)=|S|^{-1}\sum_{g\in S}\operatorname{Tr}(g)$. For $n>0$, the identity is $I^{\otimes n}$. In the ordered product basis [F5]–[F6], its trace is a sum over bit words; [F11] factors this finite sum into the product of its one-qubit diagonal sums, each equal to $2$. Thus its trace is $2^n$. When $n=0$, [F6]–[F8] give trace $1=2^0$. For $n>0$, every other $g\in S$ has nonzero binary label by [F2], hence at least one nonidentity tensor factor. By [F4] that factor is a scalar multiple of $X$, $Z$, or $XZ$. For any tensor Pauli, its trace is the sum over bit words of products of one-qubit diagonal coefficients; [F11] factors this finite sum into the product of the one-qubit traces. By [F3], $X$ and $XZ$ are off-diagonal, while $Z$ has diagonal entries $1,-1$, so the nonidentity factor has trace zero. Hence every such $g$ has trace zero. Therefore $\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_S)=2^n/|S|=2^{n-r}$.
As $\Pi_S$ is idempotent, [F9] gives $\operatorname{Tr}(\Pi_S)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{im}\Pi_S$. Combining with step 1.1 proves the dimension formula, including $r=0$ and $r=n$.

When $r=n$, step 2.1 gives a one-dimensional common fixed space, so the space is nonzero and all of its nonzero vectors determine the same ray. This is the existence and uniqueness assertion used in the definition of a pure stabilizer state.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ set

$$P_b:=\frac{I_H+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b).$$

Then $P_0,P_1$ are complementary orthogonal projections and
$p_0,p_1\ge0$, with $p_0+p_1=1$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The following are equivalent:

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be
linear. Choose any ordered basis $\mathcal B$ of $V$ and define the **trace of
the endomorphism $T$** by

$$\operatorname{tr}(T):=\operatorname{tr}([T]_{\mathcal B}^{\mathcal B}).$$

This is independent of the chosen basis: matrices of the same endomorphism in
two ordered bases are similar, and similar matrices have equal trace. When
$V$ is the zero space, the empty basis gives trace $0$.

derivations.claim: Set $Q_b=P_b\rho P_b$. For every $v$, self-adjointness of $P_b$ in [F2] gives $\langle Q_bv,v\rangle=\langle\rho P_bv,P_bv\rangle\ge0$ by [A1]. Thus $Q_b$ is nonnegative.

By [F1], [F2], and cyclicity [F3], $\operatorname{Tr}(Q_b)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_b\rho P_b) =\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b^2)=p_b=0$. By [F4], choose an orthonormal eigenbasis of $Q_b$ whose eigenvalues are nonnegative; [F5] expresses its trace as their finite sum. A finite sum of nonnegative reals is zero only when each term is zero, so $Q_b=0$.
The branch output is therefore zero. Normalization would require dividing it by $p_b=0$, which is undefined; the conditional-state convention assigns no state to this zero-probability outcome.

Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. $$\omega((x,z),(x',z')):=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'.$$

This is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form over $\mathbb F_2$; $V_n$ has dimension $2n$. In characteristic two, alternating also implies symmetry.

$P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$, with the fixed tensor order and
$X^x=\bigotimes_{j<n}X^{x_j}$, $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j<n}Z^{z_j}$. A **row**
$(k,x,z)$ is Hermitian when $k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod 2$; it stores the exact
Pauli phase as well as its binary label $(x,z)$.

For $n=0$, use the scalar Pauli convention of
[[def-qc-pauli-group-on-zero-qubits]]; the generator list is empty.

A **generator tableau** is an ordered list of $n$ Hermitian rows whose Pauli
operators commute, have linearly independent labels, and generate a subgroup
not containing $-I$. It represents the unique common $+1$ ray when the rows
stabilize a pure state. An **extended tableau** also stores Hermitian
destabilizer rows $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ and stabilizer rows $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ with

$$\omega(d_i,s_j)=\delta_{ij},\quad \omega(d_i,d_j)=0,\quad \omega(s_i,s_j)=0.$$

The exact phase and symplectic conventions are those of the cited Pauli
suppliers. The generator-only simulator uses the $s_j$ rows; the extended
pairing is retained as a second representation invariant.

Let $S$ be a stabilizer subgroup on $n\ge0$ qubits and let
$\lambda(P(k,x,z))=(x,z)$. Then $\lambda|_S$ is injective, its image $L$ is an
isotropic $\mathbb F_2$-subspace, the rank $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L$ depends only
on $S$ and not on a generating list, and
$|S|=2^{\dim_{\mathbb F_2}L}$.

Let $V=\mathbb F_2^{2n}$ have the standard symplectic form
$\omega((x,z),(x',z'))=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'$. If $L\le V$ is isotropic and
$r=\dim L$, then

$$\dim L^\perp=2n-r.$$

Consequently $r\le n$, and if $r=n$ then

$$L^\perp:=\{v\in V:\omega(v,\ell)=0\text{ for every }\ell\in L\}=L.$$

For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.
For $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z\in\mathcal P_n$, the operator is Hermitian exactly when $k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod 2$. In that case $P(k,x,z)^2=I$.

Let $S$ be a rank-$n$ stabilizer subgroup on an ordered $n$-qubit register
$H_n=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$. A **pure stabilizer state** is the unique ray
in the common $+1$ fixed space

$$\mathcal C(S):=\{\psi\in H_n:g\psi=\psi\text{ for every }g\in S\}.$$

The cited projector-rank theorem proves that this common space is nonzero and
one-dimensional, so the ray is well defined. A normalized representative may
be used for probabilities, but the state itself is the ray, not a chosen
vector.

For $k,k'\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$ and $x,z,x',z'\in\mathbb F_2^n$, with $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$ and $X^xZ^z$ ordered as written,

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=P(k+k'+2(z\cdot x'),x+x',z+z'),$$

where the dot product is first evaluated in $\mathbb F_2$ as $0$ or $1$, and then multiplied by $2$ in $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$. The set $\mathcal P_n$ is a group. If $p\in\{0,1\}$ represents $x\cdot z\in\mathbb F_2$, then $P(k,x,z)^*=P(2p-k,x,z)=P(k,x,z)^{-1}$, and its center is $Z_n=\{i^k I:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$.

Let $H_n=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$ be an ordered $n$-qubit register, let
$\rho\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ be a density operator, and let $M\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$
be a Hermitian Pauli observable with $M^2=I$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ define

$$P_b:=\frac{I+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b),\qquad \mathcal I_b(\rho):=P_b\rho P_b.$$

The outcome $b$ has probability $p_b$. Its conditional density operator is
$\rho_b:=\mathcal I_b(\rho)/p_b$ when $p_b>0$; it is $\bot$ (no assigned
conditional density operator) when $p_b=0$.
The branch map $\mathcal I_b$ is the projective measurement instrument for the
$(-1)^b$ eigenspace of $M$. A non-Hermitian phase-aware Pauli is outside this
definition. For $n\ge1$, Hermiticity of $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$ means
$k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod2$; in particular $Y=iXZ$ is admitted. For $n=0$,
the admitted observables are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$.

The hypotheses and meanings of density operator, Pauli observable, projective
measurement, POVM outcome law, and instrument are the cited suppliers. The
local projector calculation is [[lem-qc-pauli-measurement-projectors]].

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let $\psi\in H$
be a unit vector, and let $P:H\to H$ be an orthogonal projection. Under the
root-linear-first Dirac convention,

$$P|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|P=|P\psi\rangle\langle P\psi|,$$

$$\operatorname{Tr}(P|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|)
=\operatorname{Tr}(|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|P)
=\|P\psi\|^2.$$

The map $\pi:\mathcal P_n\to V_n$, $P(k,x,z)\mapsto(x,z)$, is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel exactly $Z_n$. Therefore the quotient map in [[def-qc-binary-pauli-label-and-quotient]] is an isomorphism $\mathcal P_n/Z_n\cong (V_n,+)$, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_n=2n$. No phase or label ambiguity occurs, including when $n=1$.

For nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product $H$, the map sending a ray $[u]$ to the rank-one projector $P_u=|u\rangle\langle u|$ of any unit representative is well-defined and bijective onto the rank-one orthogonal projections on $H$. Each $P_u$ is non-negative and has trace one.

The zero-qubit register is the empty tensor product $H_0=\mathbb C$ with
identity operator $I_{H_0}$. Define

$$P_0(k):=i^kI_{H_0}\quad(k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z),\qquad
\mathcal P_0:=\{P_0(k):k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}.$$

Then $P_0(k)P_0(\ell)=P_0(k+\ell)$ and $P_0(k)^*=P_0(-k)$, so
$\mathcal P_0$ is the cyclic scalar Pauli group of order four. Its Hermitian
elements are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$. The binary-label space
$\mathbb F_2^0\times\mathbb F_2^0$ is the zero space, and the label of each
$P_0(k)$ is its unique element.

Write $\mathcal Q_n$ for the ordered tensor product of $n$ copies of the two-level register from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], with $\mathcal Q_0=\mathbb C$. Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$. Each $g\in G$ has an arity $r(g)\ge1$ and a specified unitary $U_g:\mathcal Q_{r(g)}\to\mathcal Q_{r(g)}$. An operation model states which listed gates may be called and what access or cost is assigned to them; the matrix $U_g$ by itself is only the mathematical gate data.

For $n\ge0$, the circuit wire set is $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ in its displayed order and its state space is $\mathcal Q_n$. The computational basis word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})$ is assigned slot $\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$ from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so wire $0$ is the most significant bit and the empty register has its single basis vector in slot $0$.

A gate occurrence on the $n$ wires is a pair $(g,(w_0,\ldots,w_{r(g)-1}))$ with distinct wire labels $w_j\in[n]$; the tuple order is the input and output factor order of the local gate. A layer is a finite ordered list of gate occurrences whose wire supports are pairwise disjoint. A unitary circuit is a finite chronological list $L_1,\ldots,L_d$ of such layers, with $L_1$ applied first and $L_d$ last; $d=0$ is the empty circuit. Its input, output, and terminally measured wires are specified as ordered lists without repetitions in $[n]$. This syntax specifies finite data only; the semantic action of gates on the full register is defined separately.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Fix an ordered $n$-qubit register and a finite gate alphabet as in
[[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. A **finite adaptive
Pauli-measurement circuit tree** is a finite rooted tree whose leaves are
terminal and whose nonterminal nodes are of one of these two types:

1. A gate node is labelled by a gate occurrence on the ordered register and
   has one successor. Its state update is conjugation by the global unitary
   assigned to that occurrence by
   [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]].
2. A measurement node is labelled by a Hermitian Pauli observable $M$ and has
   two outgoing edges labelled $b=0,1$. On input density operator $\rho$,
   edge $b$ has weight $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$ and unnormalized
   output $P_b\rho P_b$, where $P_b=(I+(-1)^bM)/2$ as in
   [[def-qc-pauli-measurement-branch-semantics]]. Its child state is
   $P_b\rho P_b/p_b$ only if $p_b>0$; an edge of weight zero is impossible
   and has no conditional state.

The observed measurement transcript is the ordered list of measurement-edge
labels on a root-to-leaf path. The tree itself specifies every later
instruction from that observed history, so its classical control is
deterministic. A path whose edges all have positive weights has probability
equal to their product. A path passing through a zero-weight edge has
probability zero, and its descendants are not evaluated because no
conditional state is assigned. A leaf outputs its terminal state; a ray is
assigned only on a positive-probability path whose input and gate/measurement
updates remain pure.

The complementary-projector and total-probability facts for each measurement
node are supplied by [[lem-qc-pauli-measurement-projectors]]. This definition
does not identify an instrument with a POVM or require uniqueness of such a
POVM.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call unless the model explicitly combines them. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

For $n\ge0$ and a bit string $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\mathbb F_2^n$, the
basis state $|x\rangle$ has rows indexed by $a=1,\ldots,n$ given by
$s_{j+1}=(-1)^{x_j}Z_{j+1}$ and $d_{j+1}=X_{j+1}$ for each $0\le j<n$.
Their labels satisfy the extended tableau pairing conditions.

Write a Hermitian row as $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$, with $k\in\mathbb Z/4$.
In this lemma's formulas, label coordinates are numbered by Pauli wires
$a=1,\ldots,n$ in tensor order: the coordinate denoted $x_a$ (respectively
$z_a$) here is the coordinate denoted $x_{a-1}$ (respectively $z_{a-1}$)
in [[def-qc-stabilizer-tableau]]. This reindexing changes no operator or phase.
For wire $a$ with $1\le a\le n$, conjugation by $H_a$, $S_a$, and
$S^\dagger_a$ updates the row by, respectively,

$$H_a:(k,x_a,z_a)\mapsto(k+2x_az_a,z_a,x_a),$$
$$S_a:(k,x_a,z_a)\mapsto(k+x_a,x_a,z_a\oplus x_a),$$
$$S^\dagger_a:(k,x_a,z_a)\mapsto(k-x_a,x_a,z_a\oplus x_a).$$

For distinct wires $c,t$, $\operatorname{CNOT}_{c\to t}$ updates
$x_t\mapsto x_t\oplus x_c$, $z_c\mapsto z_c\oplus z_t$, with all other label
coordinates and $k$ unchanged. Applying these conjugations to every row
preserves the generator tableau and, when present, the extended pairing
invariant.

For a rank-$n$ stabilizer tableau and a Hermitian Pauli measurement $M$, the
tableau measurement rule returns exactly the projective instrument branches:
if some stabilizer row anticommutes with $M$, both bits occur with probability
$1/2$ and the pivot update represents each conditional state; if every row
commutes with $M$, the signed row product returns the unique probability-one
bit, leaves the state unchanged, and the opposite zero-probability branch has
no normalized state.

**Inputs and admissible conditions.** An integer $n\ge0$, a basis string
$x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\mathbb F_2^n$, and a finite adaptive
Pauli-measurement circuit tree on
$H_n=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$. Circuit wire labels are
$j\in[n]=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Tableau/Pauli wire labels are $a\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
with circuit wire $j$ represented by Pauli wire $a=j+1$. Unitary instructions
are $H_j,S_j,S^\dagger_j$ and
$\operatorname{CNOT}_{c\to t}$ with distinct $c,t\in[n]$. Here
$S^\dagger:=S^*$, the conjugate transpose of the matrix
$S=\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$, so $S^*=\operatorname{diag}(1,-i)$.
Measurement instructions are Hermitian phase-aware Paulis $M=P(k,u,v)$
satisfying the Hermitian phase criterion. The tree uses the branch semantics
of [[def-qc-adaptive-pauli-circuit-tree]]. Its classical bit operations are
charged separately under [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]]. A malformed
input, unsupported gate, out-of-range wire, or non-Hermitian measurement
operand returns INVALID.

**Output.** For a valid input, the sampled measurement transcript and the
final signed generator rows representing the final pure stabilizer ray.
Fair randomness is used exactly when the measured Pauli anticommutes with a
stabilizer row.

**Initialization.** For each circuit wire $j\in[n]$, store the signed
stabilizer row $s_{j+1}=(-1)^{x_j}Z_{j+1}$. The simulator stores only these
generator rows; if $n=0$, the row list is empty.

**Execution.** Set the current tree node to the root and the transcript to the
empty list. While the current node is not a leaf, perform the instruction at
that node and move to its indicated child:

1. **Gate node.** For $H_j$, $S_j$, or $S^\dagger_j$, apply
   [[lem-qc-tableau-clifford-update]] to every generator row using Pauli wire
   $j+1$. For $\operatorname{CNOT}_{c\to t}$, apply the same supplier using
   control wire $c+1$ and target wire $t+1$. Then move to the gate node's
   unique successor.
2. **Measurement node with a pivot.** Compute
   $\omega(\lambda(s_a),\lambda(M))$ for each row $a=1,\ldots,n$. If any
   value is $1$, choose the least such $a$ and retain the old row
   $g=s_a$. Sample a fair bit $b$. For every other row $s_\ell$ that
   anticommutes with $M$, replace it by the exact phase-aware product
   $s_\ell g$. Replace the pivot row by $(-1)^bM$, keep the other rows,
   append $b$ to the transcript, and move to the child edge labelled $b$.
3. **Measurement node without a pivot.** If every row commutes with $M$,
   form the augmented matrix over $\mathbb F_2$ whose columns are
   $\lambda(s_1),\ldots,\lambda(s_n)$ in the fixed $(x,z)$ coordinate order
   and whose right-hand side is $\lambda(M)$. Scan the generator columns in
   increasing order. For each column, choose the least row not already used as
   a pivot that has entry $1$ in that column, swap it into the next pivot row,
   and add that pivot row to every other row having entry $1$ in the column.
   If a column has no pivot, or a row with zero coefficient part has right-hand
   side $1$, return INVALID. Otherwise read the unique coefficient vector
   $c=(c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ from the right-hand sides of the pivot rows. For $n=0$
   this is the empty system with the empty solution. Multiply the selected
   signed rows in increasing row order using the exact phase-aware product
   rule, obtaining $G$. Set $b=0$ if $G=M$ and $b=1$ if $G=-M$; the unique
   matching sign is guaranteed by
   [[lem-qc-tableau-deterministic-sign]]. Leave the tableau unchanged, append
   $b$ to the transcript, and move to the child edge labelled $b$.

For a valid rank-$n$ pure stabilizer tableau, each deterministic system is
consistent and has full column rank. Each iteration moves to a child, and the
finite tree ensures that execution reaches a leaf. Return the transcript and
current stabilizer rows there. Correctness and resource bounds are separate
results.

The zero-qubit register is the empty tensor product $H_0=\mathbb C$ with
identity operator $I_{H_0}$. Define

$$P_0(k):=i^kI_{H_0}\quad(k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z),\qquad
\mathcal P_0:=\{P_0(k):k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}.$$

Then $P_0(k)P_0(\ell)=P_0(k+\ell)$ and $P_0(k)^*=P_0(-k)$, so
$\mathcal P_0$ is the cyclic scalar Pauli group of order four. Its Hermitian
elements are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$. The binary-label space
$\mathbb F_2^0\times\mathbb F_2^0$ is the zero space, and the label of each
$P_0(k)$ is its unique element.

This supplies the empty-register case when an item uses Pauli notation whose
general positive-wire convention is stated separately.

derivations.claim: Before the first instruction, [F5] gives a tableau for the exact input state and transcript. This establishes the simulation invariant at prefix length zero.

A gate updates at most $2n$ rows, each with $O(n)$ bits. A measurement tests at most $n$ symplectic pairings, each in $O(n)$ bit operations. In its random case it updates at most $n$ rows by an $O(n)$ Pauli product each. In its deterministic case Gaussian elimination on a $2n$-by-$n$ binary system uses $O(n^3)$ bit operations, and multiplying at most $n$ selected rows uses $O(n^2)$. Thus every quantum instruction costs $O((n+1)^3)$. Initializing and writing the $n$ signed rows each takes $O((n+1)^2)$ bit operations because each row stores $2n+O(1)$ bits; writing the transcript takes $O(T)$. Summing instruction costs over $T$ steps, then adding initialization, output, and $C_{\rm cl}$ gives $O((n+1)^2+T(n+1)^3+C_{\rm cl})$. The tableau has $O((n+1)^2)$ bits, elimination scratch has $O((n+1)^2)$ bits, and the output transcript has at most $T$ bits. The register width and controller charge use the accounting in [F4]; gate and measurement instructions are counted in $T$ and charged by the bit-operation bounds just proved.

Suppose the invariant holds after a prefix of $k$ instructions. If the next instruction is a Clifford generator, [F6] conjugates every stabilizer row by the same unitary as the circuit, whose action is ordered by [F2]. If it is a Pauli measurement, [F3] supplies the finite instrument-history branch and [F7] gives its probability and updated tableau; [F8] samples a fair bit exactly in the random case and computes the signed bit in the deterministic case. Equal transcripts therefore select the same next child by [F3]. Thus the conditional transition laws agree after instruction $k+1$. A terminated branch remains in the same final state. Each simulator iteration advances to a child of the finite tree, so it reaches a leaf after at most $T$ quantum instructions. Induction through that path proves equality of the complete transcript and final ray distributions.

If $n=0$, no wire gate is admissible and [F9] makes every valid Pauli observable $I$ or $-I$. Its label is the unique zero vector, so the empty row product determines the sign and each measurement is deterministic; the tableau uses constant space. The uniform $(n+1)$ bounds therefore include this boundary.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

Let $H_n=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$ be an ordered $n$-qubit register, let
$\rho\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ be a density operator, and let $M\in M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$
be a Hermitian Pauli observable with $M^2=I$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ define

$$P_b:=\frac{I+(-1)^bM}{2},\qquad p_b:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b),\qquad \mathcal I_b(\rho):=P_b\rho P_b.$$

The outcome $b$ has probability $p_b$. Its conditional density operator is
$\rho_b:=\mathcal I_b(\rho)/p_b$ when $p_b>0$; it is $\bot$ (no assigned
conditional density operator) when $p_b=0$.
The branch map $\mathcal I_b$ is the projective measurement instrument for the
$(-1)^b$ eigenspace of $M$. A non-Hermitian phase-aware Pauli is outside this
definition. For $n\ge1$, Hermiticity of $P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$ means
$k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod2$; in particular $Y=iXZ$ is admitted. For $n=0$,
the admitted observables are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$.

The hypotheses and meanings of density operator, Pauli observable, projective
measurement, POVM outcome law, and instrument are the cited suppliers. The
local projector calculation is [[lem-qc-pauli-measurement-projectors]].

Let $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$ be a pure stabilizer state density operator,
and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli observable that anticommutes with one of its
stabilizer generators. Then
$\operatorname{Tr}(P_0\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(P_1\rho)=1/2$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $S=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_n\rangle$ be a stabilizer
subgroup whose displayed generators have linearly independent binary labels
and fix a unit vector $\psi$ on $n$ qubits. Let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable anticommuting with $g_1$. For either outcome $b\in\{0,1\}$, define
$g'_1=(-1)^bM$ and, for $j>1$, set $g'_j=g_jg_1$ if $g_j$ anticommutes with
$M$, and $g'_j=g_j$ otherwise. Then the updated rows generate a rank-$n$
stabilizer subgroup for the normalized post-measurement state
$P_b|\psi\rangle/\|P_b|\psi\rangle\|$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, let
$\rho$ be a density operator on $H$, and let $M$ be a Hermitian Pauli
observable on $H$ with $M^2=I_H$. For $b\in\{0,1\}$ put
$P_b=(I_H+(-1)^bM)/2$ and $p_b=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho P_b)$. If $p_b=0$,
then $P_b\rho P_b=0$. The outcome has probability zero and, under the
conditional-state convention, has no normalized conditional state.

derivations.claim: The initial generator $Z$ fixes $|0\rangle$, and it anticommutes with $X$ by [F1]. Hence [F3] gives $p_0=p_1=1/2$ for the first measurement.

Directly, $P_0|0\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/2$ and $P_1|0\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/2$. Each vector has squared norm $1/2$, so normalization gives $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $|-\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$. By [F4], their stabilizers are $+X$ and $-X$, respectively.

Measuring $X$ again on either state is deterministic: $|+\rangle$ lies in $P_0H_1$ and $|-\rangle$ lies in $P_1H_1$. The opposite projector annihilates the state, so its branch has probability zero and no normalized conditional state by [F5].

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, with the root library's convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. A **density operator** on $H$ is a non-negative endomorphism $\rho:H\to H$ with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=1$; non-negative and trace have the meanings of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]] and [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]. The zero-dimensional space is excluded: its only endomorphism has trace $0$.

Here $\ker\rho=\{x\in H:\rho x=0\}$, using the kernel of a linear map from [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]. The **support** of $\rho$ is the orthogonal complement of its kernel in the root convention:

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. This restriction is an endomorphism: if $x\in S$ and $y\in\ker\rho$, self-adjointness gives $\langle\rho x,y\rangle=\langle x,\rho y\rangle=0$, so $\rho x\in(\ker\rho)^\perp=S$.

Let $F$ be a field, let $m,n,p\in\mathbb N$, and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and
$B=(b_{jk})\in M_{n\times p}(F)$. Their **matrix product** is the matrix
$AB\in M_{m\times p}(F)$ whose entries are

$$(AB)_{ik}:=\sum_{j\in n}a_{ij}b_{jk}.$$

The sum is the finite sum in the additive commutative monoid of $F$. If $n=0$,
it is the empty sum, so $AB$ is the zero matrix of shape $m$ by $p$.

The **identity matrix** $I_n\in M_n(F)$ has entry $1$ when $i=j$ and entry $0$
when $i\ne j$. In particular, $I_0$ is the unique empty matrix in $M_0(F)$.

For $A\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and $B\in M_{n\times m}(F)$,

$$\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA).$$

The two products may have different sizes, and the equality includes $m=0$ or
$n=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be linear. The following are equivalent:

1. $T$ is non-negative.
2. $T$ is self-adjoint and every eigenvalue of $T$ is a nonnegative real number.
3. Some orthonormal basis makes the matrix of $T$ diagonal with nonnegative real diagonal entries.
4. There exists a linear map $S:V\to V$ such that $T=S^*S$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ and let $T:V\to V$ be

On $V_n=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n$, with coordinate order $(x,z)$, define

$$\omega((x,z),(x',z')):=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'.$$

This is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form over $\mathbb F_2$; $V_n$ has dimension $2n$. In characteristic two, alternating also implies symmetry.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map of vector spaces over $F$, with $V$
finite-dimensional. Then

$$\dim_F V=\operatorname{nullity}T+\operatorname{rank}T.$$

Equivalently,

$$\dim_F V=\dim_F(\ker T)+\dim_F(\operatorname{im}T).$$

Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $F$ ([[def-vector-space]]) that is
finite-dimensional with $\dim_F V = n$ ([[def-dimension]]), and let $U$ be a
linear subspace of $V$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). Then

1. $U$ is finite-dimensional over $F$ and $\dim_F U \le n$;
2. $\dim_F U = n$ **if and only if** $U = V$;
3. **Extension, with no choice principle.** Every linearly independent
   $A_0 \subseteq U$ is contained in a basis of $U$: there is a basis $B$ of $U$
   with $A_0 \subseteq B \subseteq U$. Claim 1 is the case $A_0 = \varnothing$.
   Since $V$ is itself a linear subspace of $V$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]), claim 3
   applies with $V$ in place of $U$, and hence to **any** finite-dimensional
   vector space over $F$ in place of the pair $(V, U)$.

**Nothing above uses a choice principle**, and claim 3 in particular is the
finite-dimensional substitute for the Zorn-based extension theorem stated earlier
on this page. In finite dimension the extension terminates on its own, because
[[cor-independent-set-is-no-larger-than-a-finite-spanning-set]] bounds the size
of an independent set and [[thm-well-ordering-principle]] then supplies a largest
one; no selection is made anywhere.

**Finiteness is essential in claim 2.** Without it the equality case fails: the
companion page exhibits a
proper linear subspace of an infinite-dimensional space whose basis is
equinumerous with a basis of the whole space.

Assume now $n\ge1$. If $v=(x,z)\in V$ pairs to zero with every vector, pairing with $(e_j,0)$ and $(0,e_j)$ gives $z_j=x_j=0$ for every $j$. More generally, for any linear functional $\phi$ on $V$, set $a_j=\phi(e_j,0)$ and $b_j=\phi(0,e_j)$. Then $v=(b,a)$ satisfies $\omega(v,(x',z'))=b\cdot z'+a\cdot x'=\phi(x',z')$ by linearity. Thus $v\mapsto\omega(v,\cdot)$ is both injective and onto.

Put $r=\dim L$ and choose a basis $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$ of $L$. Extend it to a basis of $V$ using [F3]. For any $y\in\mathbb F_2^r$, define a linear functional on this basis by $\phi(\ell_j)=y_j$ and by zero on the added basis vectors. Step 1.2 supplies $v\in V$ with $\omega(v,\cdot)=\phi$, so $T:V\to\mathbb F_2^r$, $T(v)=(\omega(v,\ell_j))_{j=1}^r$, is onto. Its kernel is $L^\perp$, and [F2] gives $\dim L^\perp=2n-r$. This includes $r=0$, where both the basis and $\mathbb F_2^r$ are empty or zero-dimensional.

For $n\ge1$, isotropy gives $L\subseteq L^\perp$. Comparing dimensions with step 2.1 gives $r\le2n-r$, hence $r\le n$. If $r=n$, both subspaces have dimension $n$, so [F3] gives $L=L^\perp$. This argument uses only finite basis extension and no choice principle.
Step 1.1 proves the result for $n=0$, and step 1.2 and step 2.1 and step 3.1 prove it for $n\ge1$. These cases exhaust all dimensions in the Statement.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

The zero-qubit register is the empty tensor product $H_0=\mathbb C$ with
identity operator $I_{H_0}$. Define

$$P_0(k):=i^kI_{H_0}\quad(k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z),\qquad
\mathcal P_0:=\{P_0(k):k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}.$$

Then $P_0(k)P_0(\ell)=P_0(k+\ell)$ and $P_0(k)^*=P_0(-k)$, so
$\mathcal P_0$ is the cyclic scalar Pauli group of order four. Its Hermitian
elements are $I_{H_0}$ and $-I_{H_0}$. The binary-label space
$\mathbb F_2^0\times\mathbb F_2^0$ is the zero space, and the label of each
$P_0(k)$ is its unique element.

This supplies the empty-register case when an item uses Pauli notation whose
general positive-wire convention is stated separately.

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

For $n\ge0$, $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, and $k\in\mathbb Z/4$, write
$P(k,x,z)=i^kX^xZ^z$, with the fixed tensor order and
$X^x=\bigotimes_{j<n}X^{x_j}$, $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j<n}Z^{z_j}$. A **row**
$(k,x,z)$ is Hermitian when $k\equiv x\cdot z\pmod 2$; it stores the exact
Pauli phase as well as its binary label $(x,z)$.

For $n=0$, use the scalar Pauli convention of
[[def-qc-pauli-group-on-zero-qubits]]; the generator list is empty.

A **generator tableau** is an ordered list of $n$ Hermitian rows whose Pauli
operators commute, have linearly independent labels, and generate a subgroup
not containing $-I$. It represents the unique common $+1$ ray when the rows
stabilize a pure state. An **extended tableau** also stores Hermitian
destabilizer rows $d_1,\ldots,d_n$ and stabilizer rows $s_1,\ldots,s_n$ with

$$\omega(d_i,s_j)=\delta_{ij},\quad \omega(d_i,d_j)=0,\quad \omega(s_i,s_j)=0.$$

The exact phase and symplectic conventions are those of the cited Pauli
suppliers. The generator-only simulator uses the $s_j$ rows; the extended
pairing is retained as a second representation invariant.

On $V_n=\mathbb F_2^n\oplus\mathbb F_2^n$, with coordinate order $(x,z)$, define

$$\omega((x,z),(x',z')):=x\cdot z'+z\cdot x'.$$

This is a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form over $\mathbb F_2$; $V_n$ has dimension $2n$. In characteristic two, alternating also implies symmetry.

The map $\pi:\mathcal P_n\to V_n$, $P(k,x,z)\mapsto(x,z)$, is a surjective group homomorphism with kernel exactly $Z_n$. Therefore the quotient map in [[def-qc-binary-pauli-label-and-quotient]] is an isomorphism $\mathcal P_n/Z_n\cong (V_n,+)$, and $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}V_n=2n$. No phase or label ambiguity occurs, including when $n=1$.

For the matrices $X,Y,Z$ of [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], each is self-adjoint and unitary, and $X^2=Y^2=Z^2=I$. Distinct Pauli matrices anticommute. For $j,k\in\{x,y,z\}$,
$$\sigma_j\sigma_k=\delta_{jk}I+i\sum_{\ell\in\{x,y,z\}}\epsilon_{jk\ell}\sigma_\ell,\qquad \operatorname{tr}(\sigma_j\sigma_k)=2\delta_{jk}.$$
Here $\sigma_x=X,\sigma_y=Y,\sigma_z=Z$, $\delta_{jk}=1$ when $j=k$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\epsilon$ is the alternating symbol with $\epsilon_{xyz}=1$. Also $\operatorname{tr}(I)=2$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma_j)=0$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

For $a=(x,z)$ and $b=(x',z')$ in $V_n$ and any phases $k,k'$, 

$$P(k,x,z)P(k',x',z')=(-1)^{\omega(a,b)}P(k',x',z')P(k,x,z).$$

Thus the Pauli operators commute exactly when their labels are symplectically orthogonal.

The displayed tensor powers are tensor maps on the ordered factors, using [[def-qc-tensor-map]].
Fix an integer $n\ge 1$. Let $\mathcal H_n=Q_2^{\otimes n}$ be the ordered tensor register of $n$ qubits from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]], and let $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. We name the wires $1,\ldots,n$; wire $j$ is position $j-1$ in the source's $0$-based factor list. Bit tuples use the big-endian encoding from [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]], so the first wire is the most significant bit. Write $X_j$ and $Z_j$ for the tensor maps with the displayed one-qubit matrix on wire $j$ and the identity on every other wire. For $x,z\in\mathbb F_2^n$, set $X^x=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n X^{x_j}$ and $Z^z=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n Z^{z_j}$, where an exponent $0$ means the identity on that factor and an exponent $1$ means the displayed Pauli matrix. For $k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, define

$$P(k,x,z):=i^kX^xZ^z.$$

The **phase-aware $n$-qubit Pauli set** $\mathcal P_n$ is the set of these operators with matrix multiplication. Its scalar subset is $Z_n:=\{i^k I_{\mathcal H_n}:k\in\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\}$. The product-and-adjoint theorem proves that $\mathcal P_n$ is a group and that $Z_n$ is its center.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].
